title: Broccoli Mush
description:
Add the crème fraiche and puree (you can leave a few lumps if you’d like, or make it smooth).
Scrape the puree into an ovenproof serving dish. Then stir in the sour cream, Parmesan, salt, and pepper to taste, mixing well.
Bake for 25 minutes, or until the puree is steaming hot.
Garnish with reserved flowerets and serve immediately.
Well, that’s certainly not a very appetizing name, but that’s what we’ve called this favorite. Its real name is “Pureed Broccoli With Crème Fraiche” and it’s good with just about anything.
We discovered this, like so many other recipes, ideas, and good times, from The Silver Palate Cookbook. I hope you’ll explore your copy of the 25th Anniversary Edition for many more ideas, techniques, and comments than the ones we have here.
START TO FINISH: 45 MIN
Broccoli Mush
Put on a big pot of salted water to boil.
Coarsely chop the broccoli, leaving 6-8 small flowerets whole (for decoration).
Cook the broccoli in the boiling water just until barely done, probably around 6 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees.
After draining, reserve the 8 flowerets, and put the rest in a food processor (you may have to work in batches).
ingredients: 4 or more big bunches of broccoli,
½ cup or so Parmesan cheese
directions: As is the case with almost all recipes, you can play with the ingredients and proportions. If you don’t have crème fraiche, use some cream cheese; put in more sour cream if you like; add some butter; include the nutmeg or not; heat the mush more quickly in the microwave if the timing or space is an issue; have more or less or no flowerets.
